title: LC-MT365-ProjectOwnedGovernanceLifecycle
clause: Make every managed project node own its canonical taskboard, work packets and microtasks through Locus.

scope.summary: GOAL: Implement project-owned taskboard, work-packet and microtask lifecycles for every root project, subproject, task or prototype managed by Handshake. The canonical records live in SurrealDB and use project-qualified identity. Files and board views are projections. A child project can have its own complete taskboard/WP/MT graph regardless of its parent state; parent summaries are derived later by MT-366. Lifecycle operations include create, register, start, gate, block, complete, close, reopen and deletion request with typed invariants, evidence links and operator attribution.
forbidden_paths: Parent project mutating child governance through rollups
Any SQLite/PostgreSQL authority, adapter or proof fixture
acceptance_criteria: Every managed project kind can own one canonical taskboard and multiple project-qualified WPs/MTs with enforced ownership relations.
WP and MT transition tables enforce dependencies, gates, terminal states, evidence requirements and idempotent retries in real SurrealDB transactions.
Taskboard Markdown/JSON files and GUI rows are derived projections whose deletion or corruption cannot alter canonical Locus state.
A child project's governance remains independently operable when its parent is inactive, except for explicit inherited policy defined by authority.
Concurrent create/start/complete/close requests yield one canonical settlement and attributable receipts without duplicate work units.
proof_targets: Repeated-label isolation tests across parent and child projects
Concurrent lifecycle and idempotency tests with canonical reread

argus_targets: Same MT label in two projects

enforcement_boundaries: Every taskboard/WP/MT mutation verifies project membership and action authority.
Parent visibility never implies child-governance visibility.
same_project_private_resource_cases: A project member outside a private AccessSpace cannot read or mutate protected WPs, MTs or board rows.
cross_account_negative_cases: Cross-account users cannot discover project governance units through direct ids, board queries or lifecycle receipts.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Projection generation filters through the same canonical authorization context and never adds denied governance records.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Revocation or project switch invalidates board subscriptions, cached rows and mutation authority before the next operation.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Board counts, status buckets, duplicate-id errors and projection diagnostics exclude denied governance records.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Record every governance transition request, canonical revision, settlement and projection enqueue id.
Expose invalid state, ownership mismatch, projection drift and duplicate-id detection.
Record DEFERRED-with-reason if lifecycle and projection health watchers are unavailable; never silently skip.

risk_if_missed: Projects will share or lose governance state, and UI/filesystem projections can become accidental authorities.

risks: Two projects share a board record.
A projection edit changes canonical state.
Parent visibility exposes a private child MT.
minimum_controls: One-way projection generation and canonical reread.

research_provenance.source: MT-361 audit, MT-362/364 identity and lifecycle contracts, current taskboard/WP/MT workflows and SurrealDB transaction guidance.
research_provenance.selected_approach: Canonical project-owned governance records in SurrealDB with deterministic projections and typed lifecycle transitions.
